name: Drug-related Renal Tubular Dysgenesis

criteria.description: Documented prenatal or perinatal exposure to drugs known to interfere with the renin-angiotensin system (e.g., ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers)
Renal biopsy showing absence or severe hypoplasia of proximal renal tubules with preserved glomeruli
Neonatal oliguria or anuria with refractory hypotension and renal failure
Renal ultrasound demonstrating hyperechogenic kidneys with poor corticomedullary differentiation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of documented drug exposure plus clinical presentation consistent with renal tubular dysgenesis and confirmatory histopathological findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and histopathological; genetic testing typically negative as this is an acquired condition.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic early renal failure in neonates
searchTerms: very low urine output in newborn

pathognomonic.notes: Persistent low blood pressure unresponsive to standard therapy
searchTerms: low blood pressure not responding to treatment

pathognomonic.symptomName: Histopathological absence or hypoplasia of proximal renal tubules

occasional.symptomName: Electrolyte imbalances other than hyperkalemia (e.g., hyponatremia)

rare.notes: Due to fetal akinesia from oligohydramnios

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen indicating renal failure
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing hyperechogenic kidneys with poor corticomedullary differentiation
Chest X-ray or fetal ultrasound demonstrating pulmonary hypoplasia
genetic: No pathogenic variants typically identified as condition is acquired
other: Histopathology revealing absence or severe hypoplasia of proximal renal tubules with preserved glomeruli

distinguishingFeatures: Genetic mutations in renin-angiotensin system genes
Family history of renal tubular dysgenesis
Complete absence of one or both kidneys on imaging

redFlags: Severe neonatal oliguria or anuria unresponsive to fluids
Refractory hypotension in neonate despite vasopressors
History of maternal drug exposure to renin-angiotensin system inhibitors during pregnancy
references: Orphanet: Drug-related Renal Tubular Dysgenesis - ORPHA:97368
Kawasaki et al., Drug-induced renal tubular dysgenesis: clinical and pathological features, Pediatric Nephrology, 2019
Feldkamp et al., Renal tubular dysgenesis: clinical spectrum and pathogenesis, Kidney International, 2017
